title: edge shard reconciliation window mismatch causing intermittent underbilling for multi-route fanout
creator: Aisha R. Patel
description:
Summary: Some tenant organizations with high fanout routes are intermittently not having all request tokens accounted for during edge-shard reshuffles. A subset of per-key increments are being dropped from the shard-aggregate reconciliation step when window boundaries are misaligned between the ingest path and the background reconciler. This leads to underbilling and quota counters that are lower than reality for short periods (minutes to hours) depending on reshuffle cadence.

Background: The per-route/per-key meter ingestion streams into N edge shards. Each shard maintains a local rolling window (1s/1m/1h buckets) and periodically emits aggregates to the global reconciler. During traffic spikes + shard resharding (triggered by autoscale/rebalance), we observed the reconciler applying aggregates that use a different window anchor than the ingest-side emission. The reconciler deduplicator uses a (shard_id, bucket_start) key; when reassignments occur the same logical bucket can be emitted from a different shard_id before reconciliation completes. The current guard logic treats the differing shard_id as a conflicting write and silently drops the incoming aggregate if timestamp is outside the reconciler's expected window.

Why unique / not covered by existing tickets: Existing tickets focus on duplicate or double-count-overcharging and token bucket desyncs. This problem is the inverse: missing aggregates due to shard-id/window-anchor mismatch and reconciler strictness, causing undercounts. The repro pattern is tied to cross-shard fanout and dynamic shard reassignment rather than token arithmetic or credit burn races.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a test org with 3 hot routes that fan out to 5 downstream shards and enable autoscale to trigger resharding during load.
2) Generate synthetic steady traffic with periodic spikes (simulate 10k QPS bursts for 30s every 5min) across multiple API keys.
3) Observe ingest-side shard emissions (inspect /metrics/edge/emit) and the reconciler apply logs (/logs/reconciler/apply).
4) Trigger a manual shard reassignment during an emission window and watch for emitted aggregates with same bucket_start but different shard_id.
5) Note dropped apply events in reconciler logs correlated with undercount in /billing/rollup view.
6) Verify billing delta by comparing raw ingest counts (event stores) to reconciled global counters over the same timeframe.
investigation_notes: 2025-02-16: Initial report from SRE (Slack #billing-alerts) after customer escalated revenue discrepancy for org O-9384.
2025-02-17: Replayed ingest window for O-9384 in staging. Confirmed ~0.7% token delta across an 8h window coincident with two shard resizes.
2025-02-18: Debugged reconciler dedupe logic; found branch where (incoming_shard != reconciler_expected_shard) => drop if bucket_start < reconciler_clock - 1window_margin.
2025-02-19: Verified that the reconciler's expected_shard mapping is updated asynchronously via control plane; race with shard reassignment exists under rapid reshard patterns.
2025-02-24: Telemetry spike captured: reconciler_drop_events metric incremented during autoscale tests. PID trace: reconciler.v2.apply#4821.
2025-03-02: Correlated customer reports: affected orgs have multi-route fanout patterns (chat + embeddings + reranker) that concentrate emissions near the same bucket boundaries.
2025-03-03: Created initial fix branch and unit tests. Open PR and canary plan below.
proposed_fix: 1) Make reconciler dedupe key shard-agnostic: use (route_id, key_hash, bucket_start) and retain a last-applied-monotonic-sequence per logical bucket rather than per-origin shard_id.

2) Add an idempotency envelope to shard emissions containing a monotonic emission_seq and source_shard history; reconciler will accept the first valid seq and ignore duplicates irrespective of shard_id.
3) Backfill: implement a safe backfill job that replays raw ingest event logs for affected orgs to recompute global counters for the last 7 days (configurable window).
4) Add reconciliation integration tests that simulate reshard events mid-bucket and assert no net loss in reconcilied counts.
5) Expose a reconciler_drop_events alert with per-org tagging to detect recurrence quickly.
6) Short-term mitigation: loosen strict timestamp window check to allow 1 extra bucket tolerance while fix rolls out (feature flag gated).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy dedupe-key change behind feature flag to 2 reconciler replicas in staging. Run synthetic reshard load tests for 48h. (Owners: Marco Nguyen, Tanya Li)
Phase 2 (production canary): Enable feature flag for 5% of traffic routed to reconciler-variant across two regions. Monitor reconciler_drop_events, billing_rollup_deltas, and latency impact for 72h.
Phase 3 (full): Gradual rollout to 100% with backfill job running in parallel for historical correction. Schedule backfill in low-cost windows and rate-limit it to avoid overload.
Rollback: Revert feature flag and run compensating replay if we see regressions in apply latencies or double-counts.
Communication: PM to send customer notifications to affected tenants and billing team to hold automated invoices until backfill completes for high-impact orgs.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for new dedupe-key semantics (local and CI).
Chaos test harness: automated reshard + spike scenario with assertions on zero net loss and idempotency.
End-to-end validation: compare event-store raw counts vs reconciled counters via spot-check tool (script in tools/billing/reconcile_check).
Manual verification: billing run for a pilot org O-9384 to confirm corrected counters after backfill.
